Senses.Explanation: An attendant is the monastic assigned to remain close to a presiding lineage figure, carry messages, summon participants, and manage immediate needs. Chan records place attendants inside encounters as messengers, witnesses, and questioners. Senses.Explanation: Masters use the household reversal as an adverse appraisal in public exchanges and comments. It is repeatedly coupled with “point to a deer as a horse” (指鹿為馬). One address applies both verdicts even to the old advice “seek only from yourself, do not look elsewhere” (但向己求，莫從他覓); another identifies “taking the one capable of seeing and hearing as real” (認著一箇能見能聞……執以為真) as precisely mistaking servant for master. Elsewhere Xiangyan Yiduan permits bowing but warns, “you must not mistake the servant for the household head” (不得認奴作郎), while later case commentary applies the same verdict to Deshan. The ordinary status reversal becomes a portable Chan verdict on a proposed identification; which identification receives it is supplied by each passage.

Juelang Daosheng says a verse has again taken the shadow and lost the head; Miyun Yuanwu applies the phrase to someone who treats worldly busyness as an external obstacle and thereby abandons himself. Senses.Explanation: The records preserve the quoted formulation 'if what can infer is your mind, then you mistake the thief for your son,' and immediately state that 'in the patch-robed monk's gate this is called mistaking the servant for the household head' (衲僧門下謂之認奴作郎). Chan records then use the kinship error in admonition and public interview: pursuing external objects as mind is named with the phrase; an unnamed questioner asks how to judge, in darkness, mistaking thief for son and son for thief and receives 'thirty blows each'; and Huizhou Hao raises his staff and says that calling it the household head is mistaking thief for son, while denying it is fleeing the father and seeking outside. The Zen deviation is this recurrent use as a public diagnostic accusation, linked by the texts themselves to servant/master and host language. The entry reports those applications without deciding what should count as the 'true son.'
